newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Riksbank sets up US$/DEM accounts for debt office.
newsitem.headline: Riksbank sets up US$/DEM accounts for debt office.

text.p: Sweden's National Debt Office and the Riksbank said on Thursday they had decided to open U.S. dollar and German mark accounts to reduce transaction costs linked to borrowing in foreign currency.
The new accounts, to be opened at the Riksbank, will be used by the debt office from April 14 this year.
The debt office said in a statement that a substantial proportion of its foreign currency borrowing was to refinance maturing Swedish currency loans.
To date the debt office has exchanged borrowed currency immediately for Swedish crowns in the Riskbank even if the currency was intended for subsequent repayment of maturing loans.
"This has resulted in shortrun and undesired fluctuations in the composition of the debt office's foreign currency holdings," the statement said.
"The introduction of foreign currency accounts means that the debt office will have less need to make hedging transactions and can thereby cut its costs substantially."
The foreign currency accounts are to be used solely for borrowing and repayment under what is known as commercial programmes.
The maximum balance for the dollar account is US$1.5 billion and the mark account 500 million marks.
If borrowing or repayment exceeds these limits, exchange in the Riksbank will be done as it is at present.
The handling of other currrencies remains unchanged.
